title: Callable and Future
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of callable and future and identify when it is appropriate in a Java program.
Apply at least one of the lesson topics—tasks with return values—in a small, readable example.
Identify one failure, compatibility, security, or resource-management concern and describe a safe response.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study callable and future with a short explanation, an original visual map, a Java example, and a check you can perform yourself. Focus on the relationship between the rule and the behavior rather than memorizing isolated syntax.
content.why_it_matters: This concept matters because it helps you coordinate tasks without depending on unpredictable scheduling or shared mutable state. In this lesson, focus on tasks with return values and use a minimal example to check what the rule actually guarantees.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Concurrency creates ordering, cancellation, and shared-state concerns. Define task lifetime, synchronization and shutdown behavior; never rely on thread scheduling to produce a particular print order. Apply that reasoning specifically to tasks with return values and confirm the result with the example or a targeted test. The important habit is to make the assumptions explicit and use the code example as a small experiment.

items.title: Exceptions from asynchronous work
items.text: Exceptions report conditions that interrupt the normal path. Catch only when the code can recover or add context, preserve the original cause, and use try-with-resources for closeable resources.

items.title: Waiting for task completion
items.text: Use Path and Files for modern file operations, choose byte or character APIs based on the data, and close resources reliably. Parse external files defensively because their contents may be incomplete or malformed.

items.title: Cancellation and timeouts
items.text: Use the standard library type that matches the data: java.time for dates and zones, BigDecimal for exact decimal arithmetic, and locale-aware APIs for user-facing text and numbers.

content_blocks.title: Professional habit
content_blocks.text: Keep one clear hypothesis per experiment. Check the version, read the error message, test boundaries, and record what evidence supports your conclusion.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming one timing or memory observation proves a performance conclusion.
common_mistakes.why: JIT warm-up, scheduling, allocation, and workload changes can distort single measurements.
common_mistakes.fix: Use repeatable workloads and appropriate JDK diagnostics, and record the environment.

common_mistakes.problem: Testing only a single happy path.
common_mistakes.why: Boundary values and failures often reveal assumptions hidden by the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add an empty, boundary, or invalid case and state the expected behavior before running it.

common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify the actual cause of a different result.
common_mistakes.fix: Change one factor at a time and keep a short record of observed behavior.
